title: Mus'ab ibn Umayr
hookLine: a rich, perfumed youth who gave everything up and died at Uhud with a shroud too short

cards: A man who is fasting is brought his food at the end of the day, and he cannot eat it. Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf, a companion who had become wealthy, remembers a friend.
Mus'ab ibn Umayr was killed, he says, and he was better than me. All we had to wrap him in was one cloak. If we covered his head, his feet showed.
If we covered his feet, his head showed. Then the hard thing: now the world has been spread out for us, and I am afraid our good deeds were paid back early. He weeps, and leaves the food where it is.
Today: the young man in the short cloak.

teach.b: The biographers remember Mus'ab as a young man from a comfortable Meccan family, well dressed and well perfumed. Tradition says his mother cut him off when he became Muslim.
A report in Tirmidhi tells of a day he walked in wearing a cloak patched with leather, and the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, wept, remembering how he used to live.

Later, tradition says, the Prophet sent him ahead to Medina, and Sahih al-Bukhari records the people of Medina saying Mus'ab came to them with another companion, teaching them the Qur'an, before the Prophet arrived.
The young man who had everything became a teacher in a city not his own.

teach.h: KILLED AT UHUD WITH ONE CLOAK.
teach.b: Then Uhud, where Mus'ab was killed. Another companion, Khabbab, tells what happened next, also in Bukhari. Some of us died before taking any of their reward in this world, Khabbab says, and Mus'ab was one of them.
He left nothing but a striped woolen cloak, too short to cover him.
So the Prophet told them: cover his head, and lay some sweet-smelling grass, idhkhir, over his feet. A youth known for his perfume, and a body covered at the feet with wild grass.
Khabbab sets him against those who lived on and saw their fruit ripen. Mus'ab never saw it ripen. Abdur-Rahman, years later, could not eat for thinking of him.
The short cloak became a measure. Not a judgment on wealth, since Abdur-Rahman was wealthy too and is honored, but a question he kept asking himself: what was given up, and what was kept back?

how: Muslims retell the story of Mus'ab ibn Umayr, from the hadith of Khabbab and of Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf in Sahih al-Bukhari, as a reminder of what the early believers gave up.

o: the first man to build a mosque in Medina
a wealthy companion who wept and could not eat
a comfortable youth who taught Medina, killed at Uhud

games.q: Mus'ab ibn Umayr — tap the pairs.
p: where he went to teach the Qur'an

s: Mus'ab was poor all his life
the biographers remember a comfortable, well-dressed young man who gave that life up.
his one cloak could not cover both his head and his feet
so they covered his head and laid idhkhir grass over his feet.
Abdur-Rahman told the story to boast of his own wealth
he told it weeping, afraid his reward had come early.

games.q: Mus'ab has been killed at Uhud. there is one striped cloak. cover his head and his feet show; cover his feet and his head shows. what do you do?
o: cover his head, and lay grass over his feet.
cut the cloak to cover both.
games.why: Khabbab says the Prophet told them to cover his head and put idhkhir grass over his feet. the young man once known for perfume was buried under wild grass.

practice: Run through the small comforts in your day, the extra coffee, the scrolling before sleep, and choose one to set down, not as a punishment but to notice how much you carry.
If you pray, give thanks for what you have and ask for a heart that holds it lightly.

wordCard.voice: Mus'ab, who left comfort behind, taught the Qur'an in Medina, and was buried at Uhud in a cloak too short. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: a striped woolen cloak, the word Khabbab uses for all Mus'ab left behind.

carryVoice: Your line: the shroud was too short. A friend, remembered at a full table. Until tomorrow.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 1276 (Khabbab: Mus'ab killed at Uhud, the short namirah, grass over his feet)
Sahih al-Bukhari 1274 (Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf, fasting, remembers Mus'ab's shroud and weeps)
Sahih al-Bukhari 3925 (Mus'ab comes to Medina teaching the Qur'an)
Jami' at-Tirmidhi 2476 (Mus'ab in a patched cloak; the Prophet weeps remembering his former life)
